result.comment: Completed a three-story plan: recoverable story activity; Plan agents and DOT package; production wiring and retirement of obsolete default Plan paths. No owner questions remain. Retirement is owner-confirmed closure as not planned; supported legacy compatibility is retained explicitly. Publication, readiness and save remain factory-owned and are not claimed by this proposal.

plan.summary: Deliver a runnable human-led Plan workflow in three stories. Publish usable drafts as stable sub-issues, shape technical choices and acceptance in distinct conversations, preserve independent story progress and exact approvals, then reuse existing final publication/readiness controls. Activate the neutral DOT/agent package and retire obsolete default Plan code while preserving explicitly inventoried supported legacy routes.

stories.title: Manage planning sub-issues through a recoverable story activity

user_story.want: usable story drafts to become stable sub-issues that can be revised or retired safely
user_story.benefit: I can shape each story in its own discussion without losing edits or creating duplicates
notes: Drafts may omit technical design, tasks and acceptance criteria until later planning stages.
Retirement means explicit owner-confirmed closure as not planned, preserving discussion and history.

acceptance_criteria.text: Register exactly one new activity, lf_plan_story, with bounded structured create/update/retire inputs. Bind targets to the admitted parent and selected story through factory authority; reject malformed stage payloads, duplicate identities, foreign targets and unsupported operations before remote effects.

A usable initial actor/need/benefit draft can create and attach a sub-issue without architecture, tasks or acceptance criteria. Later updates preserve its stable story key and issue identity, retain stage/candidate provenance, and never classify draft publication as complete-plan readiness.

Persist immutable candidate/effect history and request correlation before forge mutation. Distinguish applied, conflict, failed and uncertain effects; after restart or lost replies, reconcile the same request. A known created issue survives attachment failure and is attached on recovery without duplicate creation; unresolved create results never trigger blind recreation.

Updates validate observed parent/provenance and expected content revision, preserve owner edits and expose conflicts for reconciliation. Observed closure, deletion or reparenting holds the affected story. Unobservable concurrent-edit races are reported as uncertainty rather than an atomic compare-and-swap guarantee.

Retirement requires authenticated owner confirmation bound to the exact active story and displayed candidate. Close with not-planned semantics, preserve issue/history and replacement references, and reject unconfirmed, stale, foreign or already-conflicting retirement requests. Architecture advice alone cannot retire a story.

Provide durable draft/candidate and effect records using store-owned SQL and an embedded migration; keep incomplete drafts distinct from complete/frozen implementation story contracts. Existing complete-story validation remains unchanged in strength.

Passing handler tests and real migrated SQLite plus controlled HTTP forge tests cover create/attach/update/retire, malformed/unauthorized inputs, stale revisions, partial attachment, lost mutation replies, restart/replay and remote drift, asserting both retained identity and honest effect state. Execute ordinary Go tests without integration tags or special Integration names.

tasks.description: Define bounded activity/stage schemas and immutable draft/effect storage, with migration and exact operation/candidate correlation.
Implement and register create, attach, update and owner-confirmed not-planned retirement through existing forge boundaries and durable reconciliation.
Write and run pure validation and handler tests with handwritten fakes for authority, stage shape, conflict and uncertainty.
Write and run real-store and controlled-forge failure/recovery tests, including migration, lost create response and create-before-attachment crash.

architecture.summary: Add a Plan-scoped effect owner to the existing graph engine; persist candidates and operations separately from complete-story publication. GitHub remains the editable story surface; retained candidates are snapshots, not another editable source.

stories.title: Deliver the three-stage Plan agents and DOT workflow package

user_story.want: focused story, technical and completion conversations with clear review points
user_story.benefit: I can guide the plan progressively and retain settled answers while different stories move at their own pace
notes: The first conversation covers only who needs what and why.
Acceptance criteria and assembled-plan approval belong to the same third stage, with no fourth stage.

acceptance_criteria.text: Ship plan.dot, three small role Markdown files, one shared Plan evidence/result contract and focused story/technical/acceptance skills under neutral teams/source assets, matching the existing Research package organization. Every referenced resource is present in the captured runtime closure; Research agents and installed .claude/.codex trees remain unchanged.

The story role produces usable actor/need/benefit drafts and scoped questions without architecture, tasks or acceptance criteria. It uses lf_plan_story to publish usable drafts and keeps story-specific content/reviews on the story sub-issue; parent content is limited to index, shared decisions and assembled review.

The technical role evaluates approved intent for reuse, architecture fit, interfaces, permissions, entities/relationships, invariants, dependencies and failure behavior, preserving decisions and assumptions. It proposes revisions or retirement when intent is infeasible or irrelevant; it does not itself approve or retire a story.

The acceptance role proposes observable criteria with stable explicit criterion IDs, proof methods and complete task-to-criterion links; it assembles the complete typed plan for the third-stage review. Its contract distinguishes future completion obligations from executed evidence and binds review to the current story/dependency/shared-decision set.

The DOT graph uses existing agent/branch/loop/ask/comment controls plus lf_plan_story. Review-ready output, questions and explicit owner promotion are distinct; every cycle has a positive bound and exhausted loops stop resumably without granting approval. It permits policy-selected eligible stories rather than requiring all stories to advance in lockstep.

The package preserves decisions, assumptions, unanswered questions and exact candidate references across replies/restarts, reuses settled answers, and specifies stale/ambiguous/mixed approval handling and routing to the earliest affected stage. Roles cannot choose modes, forge authority, credentials or implementation freeze.

Capture and package the complete runtime closure with bounded resource references and digest coverage. Passing graph/parser/schema, resource-closure and in-memory native-render tests for both supported harnesses verify stage/gate contracts and fail on missing or invalid resources; no installed-tree writes or authentic provider-execution claim is required.

Write and run graph, resource and native-render contract tests, covering positive gates, bounded loops, malformed outputs and Research behavior preservation.

stories.title: Activate the Plan workflow and retire obsolete Plan dispatch

user_story.want: the new planning conversations to run reliably in the factory and replace the old default route
user_story.benefit: I can work through story sub-issues, resume safely and know when the complete plan is ready for implementation
notes: Existing active plans retain the compatibility required by their persisted state.
Default adoption and removal of obsolete code require separate evidence; retained compatibility is explicitly inventoried.

acceptance_criteria.text: New eligible Plan runs use the captured Plan graph through the shared workflow engine and a dedicated Plan policy/decoder. Persist workflow selection separately from content/submission and implementation-workflow versions; existing active legacy runs/replans/restarts retain their admitted route unless explicitly upgraded through supported admission. Ordinary replies never select another mode.

Persist each story's stage, immutable candidates, exact upstream/shared-decision references, approvals and wait correlation. Authenticated child replies route to the matching story/stage/candidate; direct owner edits become reconciled candidate changes. Questions, unauthorized/stale/ambiguous or mixed change-and-approval replies and loop exhaustion cannot promote. Restart restores the exact wait and consumed-reply/effect state.

A scenario with three stories advances two independent stories while one remains in shaping. An intent change reopens the changed story from stage one; a technical change reopens from stage two. Traverse recorded dependencies to reopen affected downstream approvals, preserve demonstrably unrelated approvals, and hold uncertain impact for explicit resolution. Presentation-only changes preserve canonical approvals; canonical set/shared-decision changes invalidate assembled approval.

Technical shaping may propose owner-confirmed retirement via lf_plan_story; retired scope preserves history and is excluded explicitly. Revalidate remaining dependencies, replacements and final scope, blocking empty active plans, cycles, dangling/retired references, unresolved material questions or pending edits/effects.

Third-stage approval binds the exact complete current active story set and shared decisions with no fourth stage. Complete typed validation requires all story sections, stable criteria, task links and valid dependencies. Final handoff reuses already-created draft issue identities, renders the shared plan_brief.md with link-only index, and requires confirmed publication plus successful save before readiness. Input acknowledgment, draft publication, local stage approval and pending effects cannot freeze implementation scope or establish readiness.

Inventory old Plan dispatch, source instructions and compatibility handlers. Remove replaced default dispatch and genuinely unused neutral sources/references; retain required legacy readers, saved contexts and pending-effect recovery with the exact supported cohort and removal prerequisite documented. Tests prove removed paths are not selected for new admitted Plan and retained cohorts still resume. Do not claim required retained paths or external evidence prerequisites are retired.

Reconcile project documentation and affected tests with a narrow CONC-22 amendment allowing incomplete draft sub-issue publication only for admitted graph Plan while unready; legacy discussion remains nonpublishing. Preserve Research behavior and its existing activation/evidence gate, existing complete-publication safeguards and the distinction between Plan approval, implementation completion and acceptance.

Passing unit and real-store/controlled-forge/temporary-git workflow tests cover independent progress, stale and wrong-story approvals, dependent versus unrelated changes, retirement, restart at owner wait and partial publication, lost responses, save failure and legacy resume. Execute repository make check successfully after combined changes, retaining actual output; do not write dist, restart the daemon or claim offline fixtures satisfy authentic hosted/provider observations.

tasks.description: Wire dedicated Plan policy, result decoding, admission and default dispatch into existing execution/constructor seams with persisted selection.
Implement durable per-story scheduling, owner child-reply/direct-edit admission, exact approvals and dependency-aware invalidation.
Assemble approved typed stories and exact third-stage final scope; reuse draft issue identities through publication, shared index and save/readiness controls.
Inventory and remove obsolete default paths/unused neutral sources, document retained compatibility prerequisites and amend CONC-22 narrowly.
Write and run policy/decoder/approval/invalidation and legacy-dispatch unit regressions.
Write and run real SQLite, controlled HTTP forge and temporary git workflow/recovery fixtures including independent progress and failed save.
Run make check for the combined feature and retain factual results, resolving failures without touching dist or the running daemon.

architecture.summary: Activate Plan as a policy over shared graph execution, with per-story durable scheduling independent of the parent cursor. Keep stage approval separate from final managed implementation freeze and reuse the existing complete-plan publication owner.
